newsitem.title: INDIA: India extends federal rule in key state.
newsitem.headline: India extends federal rule in key state.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma issued an order on Thursday to extend New Delhi's direct rule in the country's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh following inconclusive local polls there, news agencies said.
The Press Trust of India said Sharma signed the proclamation just hours before direct rule, imposed in the politically volatile state last year, was due to expire at midnight.
Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet earlier on Thursday recommended extension of federal rule in the state where local polls last week left three political groupings deadlocked.
The agency did not say for how long direct rule over Uttar Pradesh would be extended.
The Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) emerged from the elections as the largest single party with 177 seats, well short of a majority in the 425-seat state assembly.
Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, led by federal Defence Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav, ended second with 134 seats.
The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) of former chief minister Mayawati (Eds: one name), representing the lowest Hindu castes, won 67 seats, while its Congress party ally clinched 33.
No party or alliance has been able to form a coalition to stake a viable claim to form a government in Uttar Pradesh.

News agencies said India's Election Commission issued a notification on Thursday "constituting" the newly elected state assembly to enable the formation of a government after negotiations between the rival parties.
The BJP, which built its national foundations on a Hindu revivalist agenda in Uttar Pradesh in the late 1980s, had hoped to win control of the state, which is India's biggest electoral prize.

It briefly held power in the state in 1991. But after Hindu zealots demolished a mosque in Ayodhya in December 1992, then prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao sacked four BJP state governments, including the one ruling Uttar Pradesh.
The BJP's rivals call the party "communal" because it alienates minority Moslems.
The BJP has complained that Uttar Pradesh governor Romesh Bhandari is playing a partisan role by not inviting it to form a government.

The BJP planned to hold a demostration outside the Uttar Pradesh governor's residence in Lucknow to protest against New Delhi's decision to impose federal rule, party officials in Lucknow, the state capital, said.
The Congress also criticised Deve Gowda's United Front decision to extend federal rule.

"We disapprove of the decision of the United Front government to extend President's rule in Uttar Pradesh. It is doubtful whether constitutionally the decision is justified," party spokesman V.N. Gadgil said.
